title: The Proposition
logline: Archie pitches a three-way business, and James, turning an ordinary hourglass, makes everyone wait and sets the price of his signature: proof first. The visual arc moves from Archie's room to James's bench. The hourglass is the clock all three are now on.
questions: The hourglass is new and shows up in 6 biz events (proposition, owen, partnership, production, put_to_work, closing), so whatever S2 draws becomes canon. Proposal: palm-sized, a worn brass frame with three turned posts, clear glass, pale grey-white sand. Not gold sand, so it can't be read as calc. Not glowing, so it can't be read as Rewind (biz-act1-vision says it's ordinary). OK?

Set: these shots reuse James's unit as drawn in james_meeting card5/7 and james_motion card3. That's the narrow room seen from the door, jar shelves and workbench on the right with a green-shade lamp, bookcase and coat hooks on the left, window on the right. Archie goes left by the coat hooks, as far from the jar shelves as that narrow room allows. James goes right at his bench. That fixes the 180° line for the whole biz chain.
Time of day isn't in the text. Proposal: weekday afternoon, window daylight from screen-right plus the bench lamp on, matching the existing unit art.
Player face: same open question as the col_a2 board. This board assumes 'you' stay faceless (POV only).

S5 shows James already back at his glue on card 11, one card before card 12 says so. The alternative is to show James with his hand still on the hourglass, then return to S2 (free) at card 12. I recommend keeping S5 as briefed: the ending lands on Archie treating silence as a yes, and the insert can't show that.

Budget: 5 shots across 12 cards. This is the chain opener, and S1/S2 become reusable set and prop references for 5 more events in the same room. A leaner board would cut S3 and let S4 start at card 5, but that loses the moment James's attention moves from Archie to you.

cards.text: James answers the door and shows you inside. Archie is already there, standing well back from the shelves, the way he always does - partly the allergy, partly James.
cards.why: Arrival in a known set. Card 1 can't be blank. Archie's distance from the shelves is the beat, and it carries the whole pitch.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Right. Before James starts: you've got two veins going. Two's not a hobby. Two's a supply."
cards.why: Archie is S1's focal figure, framed to read at MS scale. His pitch plays over his own spot by the wall.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "So here's the pitch. I sell. James makes. You grow it. Everyone does one job properly instead of three badly, and we split what comes in."
cards.why: Same pitch, same moment. A new line from the same speaker doesn't earn a cut.

cards.text: James has a small brass hourglass on the workbench. He turns it over while Archie talks, and again when Archie stops. It is an ordinary hourglass you've seen him use to time glue.
cards.why: A new important prop and a decisive small action. It's cheap to make and becomes the motif for the whole chain.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "You are proposing that I go into business with a man who cannot stand within two metres of his own product, and someone I taught to make a pearl."
cards.why: Power flips to James. An OTS past Archie keeps the man being described in frame.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "When you say it like that it sounds bad."
cards.why: Archie's shoulder is in the foreground, so the speaker is present. The joke lands on James's unmoved face.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "I have my own business. It carries on whatever I decide here; my clients have no interest in who your friends are. If I put my name to a second business, I want two things first."
cards.why: The turn: James stops answering Archie and sets terms to you. Spend the strongest frame here: POV, MCU, eye contact.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "One: a market that pays reliably. Three orders delivered in full. Not most of an order - in full. Whatever you have already delivered counts. I have no wish to watch you repeat yourself."
cards.why: Terms are dialogue inside the same moment. Hold.

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "Two: a serious investment. Anyone can sell a few jars. I want to see you put money into this that you would miss."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Market and money. Done." He's already on his phone, then says to you, "I'll send you proper orders - buyers I know pay. They'll come through on BizBrief."
cards.why: A decisive physical change: Archie is already on his phone. He has taken a non-answer as a deal, and the frame has to show it.

cards.text: James turns the hourglass once more and goes back to his glue. He has not said yes. He has not said no, either, and Archie is treating that as a signature.
cards.why: S5 already shows James at his glue and Archie on his phone. The resolution's whole sentence is in the frame.

shots.title: Archie against the far wall
shots.job: Place the meeting in James's known unit, and show Archie keeping as far from the stock as the room allows, plus the friction between him and James.
shots.instant: Just inside the door. James is walking ahead toward his bench with his back half to camera, one hand gesturing you in. Archie stands pressed against the left wall by the coat hooks, arms folded, mid-sentence, looking at you.
shots.framing: MWS, eye level, from the doorway (player POV, nothing of the player visible). Tighter than the existing unit wides, so Archie reads at roughly waist-up scale.
shots.composition: Archie midground screen-left by the coat hooks and chair, as the focal figure. James midground screen-right heading to the bench, three-quarter back view. Jar shelves are upper right, clearly on the opposite side from Archie, and the empty floor between them is the point.
shots.light: Weekday afternoon. Window daylight from screen-right, green-shade bench lamp on. Warm interior as in the existing unit art. No calc glow.
shots.crop: Archie's face and folded arms sit in the centre-left of the safe zone. The jar shelves stay inside the 80% width so the gap reads on small phones.
shots.unseen: The hourglass: if it's on the bench at all, keep it tiny and unlit, not a feature (it's revealed on card 4). No player body.

shots.title: Insert: the hourglass turned
shots.job: Introduce the hourglass as an ordinary object James uses to make people wait. It becomes the chain's motif.
shots.instant: James's hand has just set the hourglass down upside-down. Sand has started falling in a thin stream and the top bulb is still full.
shots.framing: Insert, CU, slight high angle onto the workbench.
shots.composition: The hourglass is centred. James's hand (old, slightly veined, light-blue shirt cuff) is lifting away from it on screen-right. Bench clutter is soft around it: glue pot with brush, tweezers, a jar lid. Archie is out of focus far back left, at most a dark olive shape.
shots.light: Bench lamp from upper right and window daylight. Brass picks up warm highlights. The sand is pale grey-white, never gold.
shots.crop: The hourglass and hand fill the central safe zone. Clutter goes to the edges.
shots.unseen: Any glow, gold or magic on the hourglass. Faces.

shots.title: James over his glasses, past Archie
shots.job: Power moves to James: he takes the pitch apart, dryly, to Archie's face.
shots.instant: James is seated on his bench stool, turned toward Archie, looking at him over the top of his glasses, one hand resting beside the running hourglass. Archie, in the foreground, has just opened his hands in a 'come on' shrug.
shots.framing: OTS from behind Archie's left shoulder, MS on James. Eye level, or very slightly low on James.
shots.composition: Archie's shoulder and curly back-of-head in the soft foreground at screen-left (olive jacket). James at screen-right midground at the bench, with the jar shelves above and behind him. 180°: Archie stays left, James right.
shots.light: Same as S1. The bench lamp gives James a warm key from upper right, and Archie's shoulder is a darker foreground silhouette.
shots.crop: James's face and the hourglass sit in the central safe zone. Archie's shoulder can bleed off the left edge.
shots.unseen: The player. Archie's face (back of head only).

shots.title: James sets the terms
shots.job: The turn: James stops answering Archie and addresses you. He sets the price of his name.
shots.instant: James is turned fully toward camera on the stool, glasses pushed up, hands flat on his knees or the bench edge, looking straight at you. This is the moment he says 'two things'. The hourglass beside him is half run through.
shots.framing: MCU, player POV, very slightly low angle so he has the weight. The 'serious investment' look.
shots.composition: James's face is centred, slightly right of centre, and the hourglass is visible at the screen-right edge of the bench. The background is the jar shelves, softened. Archie is not in frame.
shots.light: Bench lamp key from upper right. Window daylight fills on the same side. The face reads clearly at phone size.
shots.crop: Face in the upper-middle of the safe zone. Nothing story-critical in the bottom 15%.
shots.unseen: Archie, the player, and any money or contract props. The terms are in the text.

shots.title: Archie takes silence as a yes
shots.job: Payoff: James hasn't agreed, and Archie is already running the business.
shots.instant: James is bent back over his work in the foreground, brush in the glue pot, not looking up, and the hourglass has been freshly turned beside him. Behind him Archie has his phone up and is thumbing it, grinning, and glancing over it toward camera.
shots.framing: MWS two-shot, eye level, from the bench end of the room.
shots.composition: James foreground screen-right in profile at the bench. Archie background screen-left, still by the far wall at his usual distance, phone screen lit with plain shapes. The hourglass sits between them on the bench, roughly central. 180° kept.
shots.light: Same afternoon light. The phone screen gives Archie a small cool light. Warm bench lamp on James.
shots.crop: Both heads and the hourglass inside the central 60% of height. Archie's phone and face stay clear of the edges.
shots.unseen: Legible text on the phone (BizBrief appears as a blank card shape at most). Any handshake, paper or signature.
